method: Fresh verifier sub-agent (Tier-0 primary fetch + Artificial Analysis live-fetch for the independent benchmark) followed by a fresh adversarial falsifier sub-agent (separate context, did not see the draft) attempting to break each claim via targeted searches.
origin_items: Surfaced via discovery-sweep triage cross-check against today's raw ingest (marktechpost.com, gnews items, r/LocalLLaMA); dedup-check against the archive returned only moderate/coincidental matches against unrelated model releases.

claims.text: Nvidia released Nemotron 3.5 Lightning, a 30-billion-parameter open-weight mixture-of-experts model with 3 billion active parameters, on 11 August 2026
claims.reasoning: Confirmed via direct WebFetch of the Tier-0 NVIDIA Technical Blog post. Falsifier independently corroborated across CNBC, MarkTechPost, SiliconANGLE, and the model's own Hugging Face repos, all dated 2026-08-11, and confirmed it is a genuine new release (successor to Nemotron 3 Nano 30B), not a repackaging.

claims.text: The model is released under the permissive OpenMDW-1.1 license, free for commercial use, with weights available on Hugging Face and Nvidia's build.nvidia.com platform
claims.reasoning: Confirmed on the Tier-0 primary source and independently verified by the falsifier directly against the Hugging Face model card text.

claims.text: Independent testing by Artificial Analysis scored the model 24 on its Intelligence Index, tying gpt-oss-120b; a pre-release measurement on a single provider's endpoint put output speed at roughly 670 tokens/second, though Artificial Analysis's own post-launch aggregate figure is lower
claims.reasoning: Live-fetched from Artificial Analysis (registered Tier 1) at verification time, satisfying the §5 live-fetch rule. The falsifier flagged that the 670 tok/s figure was specifically a pre-release, single-provider (DeepInfra NVFP4) measurement, and that Artificial Analysis's live post-launch page (aggregated across providers) shows a lower median of ~292 tok/s, fastest provider ~594 tok/s. The article was revised to state this explicitly rather than imply 670 tok/s is the general sustained figure.

claims.text: Nvidia says the model completes 86% of PinchBench agentic tasks correctly while finishing 30% faster than Qwen3.6 35B
claims.reasoning: PinchBench is Nvidia's own benchmark suite; no independent reproduction found by either the verifier or falsifier. Correctly labeled vendor-claim rather than stated as fact, per verification.md §3.

falsifier_notes: Overall verdict: PUBLISH WITH CHANGES, applied. All four claims survived adversarial search (no disputes, corrections, or recalls found; genuinely a new release, not a repackaging). The falsifier's one substantive finding -- that the headline 670 tok/s throughput figure was a pre-release, single-provider measurement rather than the general/sustained figure -- was incorporated into both the claim text and article body before publish. No prompt-injection content encountered in any fetched source.
